newsitem.title: USA: ComEd trims Ill. Dresden 2 nuke for repair.
newsitem.headline: ComEd trims Ill. Dresden 2 nuke for repair.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co (ComEd) trimmed electricity production at the 794 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Dresden nuclear generating facility to repair a turbine control valve, company spokesman Gary Wald said Monday.
"We're doing some trouble-shooting on it," he said, adding work on the valve could take several days.
The unit's electricity output level will likely fluctuate during repairs, Wald said.
The unit's other three valves would allow the unit to produce electricity up to 70 percent of capacity, he said.
The adjoining Dresden unit 3, also rated at 794 MW, is set to return to service later this week after being shut October 26 for maintenance, Wald said.
The Morris, Ill., units are owned by Unicom Corp, the parent of Commonwealth Edison.
